hypothesis: Modelling the onset roll as a DISCRETE Bernoulli field -- corrupt by surviving active onsets to silence, generate by revealing onsets from silence with class-balanced occupancy prediction -- fixes the phase-10 failure (a continuous Gaussian DDPM decoded ~200x too dense and lost to persistence). The discrete denoiser should reconstruct masked measures of held-out scores better than silence / marginal / persistence on both validation and the unseen-lineage test split, and generate unconditionally at a density and repetition close to authentic.

representation.note: Identical roll, families, and lineage splits as fractal_denoise_v1; only the diffusion formulation changes.

model.forward_process: independent onset survival to silence with cosine abar (abar: ~1 clean -> ~0 silence)
model.reverse_process: reveal-from-silence: predict occupancy p(x0=1|xt,t), reveal a schedule-controlled fraction of silent cells, keep survivors

training.split_source: manifest lineage split (train 79 / validation 16 / test 15 scores)

task.name: masked_measure_reconstruction
task.conditioning: context onsets held active every reverse step (RePaint-style anchor)

honesty: Persistence (time-copy) on the unseen-lineage test split is the mandatory bar; phase-10 persistence was val F1 0.185 / test F1 0.109 under this exact harness.
Active-cell F1 on masked cells only; accuracy is meaningless on a 99.8%-empty roll.
Unconditional samples must land in the authentic density/repetition band; a model can win masked-F1 by copying anchored context yet still fail to generate, so both gates are reported.
This remains a generation primitive: no critic, selection policy, RL reward, or materialized audition is claimed here.
